articles.title: Education minister steps down amid Suneung-related controversies
South Korean education minister offers to resign amid AI-assisted cheating controversy
KI-Betrug bei Prüfungen: Südkoreas Bildungsminister zurückgetreten

facts.text: Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin offered his resignation on Sunday, saying he will take responsibility for the confusion sparked by last-minute changes to prevent artificial intelligence-related cheating on the annual College Scholastic Ability Test, or Suneung.

The government implemented several anti-cheating measures to prevent AI-powered cheating on the state-issued college entrance exam, including unscheduled emergency alerts sent to detect hidden smartphones.
President Lee Jae Myung accepted Choi's resignation an hour after he presented it, according to Cheong Wa Dae.

This year's Senueng was marred by fears related to cheating with AI-powered technology, after the top scorer in the national tax accountant certification examination admitted to AI-assisted cheating just before the college entrance exam.

The education authorities stepped up security measures against smart devices, leading to 111 test-takers being caught possessing or using smart devices during the exam. This included the use of smart glasses in one case and a miniature camera and wireless earphones in another.
The Education Ministry's examination misconduct committee has been reviewing the cheating cases, and will decide on penalties before the scores are released on Dec. 11.
The government and the ruling Democratic Party of Korea have suggested extending the ban for AI-assisted cheating to 10 years, potentially applying it retroactively to this year's exam.

The authorities are also mulling a review of past college entrance exams for possible AI-assisted cheating, based on credible tips. Exam papers are mandated to be stored at test locations for at least a year.
A total of 551,864 candidates registered for this year's test, which was held at 1,312 examination centres nationwide.
It also intends to offer rewards of up to 100 million won ($75,000) for reports of cheating.

stories.title: Meta says it is re-evaluating its 2030 net-zero goal as AI data centers push emissions up 45%

facts.text: Meta acknowledges that it’s time to consider whether timelines for its long-term and short-term reduction targets should be updated.
The company’s net carbon footprint — which includes the impact of contractual instruments — jumped 45 percent last year, reaching 11.9 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (mtCO2e).
Meta’s location-based emissions inventory was almost twice that amount: 21.7 million mtCO2e.

“We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net-zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets — so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year.”
Peterson and Swedeen did not provide a timeline for disclosing decisions related to that evaluation
That mirrors a 35 percent increase in power consumption, driven by new data centers.
Microsoft’s footprint jumped 25 percent; Amazon posted a 16 percent increase (including its e-commerce network); and Google disclosed an 18 percent year-over-year bump.
Meta is the first of the foursome to publicly state it will reconsider its timelines.

articles.title: AI claimed a solution to the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis — and a human did, too

facts.text: The mathematician saw his employer, Anthropic, become the first publicly traded frontier AI lab. He also appears to have solved one of the most important problems in mathematics.
The hypothesis conjectures that there is a hidden structure underlying the appearance of prime numbers.
“The precise timing is horrible,” he wrote in an essay announcing his findings
which dates back to 1859 and is among the Millennium Prize math problems.
Levent Alpöge, hauptberuflich beim KI-Unternehmen Anthropic tätig, hat einen möglichen Beweis der Riemannschen Vermutung angekündigt.
Erste unabhängige Prüfungen zeigen, dass der Lean-Code fehlerfrei kompiliert und von zwei unabhängig entwickelten Lean-Kerneln akzeptiert wird.
Eine allgemein anerkannte Lösung liegt damit noch nicht vor.
Für eine anerkannte Lösung ist ein Preisgeld von einer Million US-Dollar ausgelobt.
Mathematiker haben inzwischen mindestens zehn Billionen nichttrivialer Nullstellen berechnet, und alle liegen auf der ½-Linie.

articles.title: OpenAI research agents cost $2,400 a day per researcher, report says
오픈AI "AI가 연구 작업 절반 스스로 완료"…7개월 만에 성공률 2배

facts.text: OpenAI says its coding agents now complete 46% of research tasks that would take a person two to four hours, with no human help. In March the figure was 23%.
For tasks of four to eight hours, success rose from 13% to 35%.
At API list prices, the median OpenAI researcher used about $2,400 of agent time a day in October. That is up 62% from $1,500 in September.
Measured in time, agent use per researcher rose elevenfold, from 0.5 to 5.7 “agent workdays” a day.
Agents succeeded alone 79% of the time when monitoring training runs, and 72% when answering technical questions. They managed 25% when writing code for inference and serving systems
OpenAI says labs should be required to track and publicly report signs of recursive self-improvement
In interviews, researchers said agents still have poor taste in research ideas, code, data and writing, and need close oversight.
OpenAI flags a caveat in its own numbers. As agents improved, researchers may have changed which tasks they handed over

stories.note: Korean secondhand write-up (AI타임스, 08:25Z today) readable and adds: 4-8h tasks 13% to 35%; monitoring training anomalies 79%, launching training runs 35%; 0.5 to 5.7 agent-days per researcher; report only covers OpenAI internal research use. facts.text: 스페이스X에 수백억달러 규모의 GPU 구매 자금을 제공하는 채권단이 담보 회수가 어렵다는 이유로 반도체의 우주 반입을 제한하려 한 것으로 알려져

스페이스X가 지난 10월 발표한 약 400억달러 규모의 GPU 금융리스 약정과 관련된 것이다.
자금은 엔비디아의 차세대 '베라 루빈' GPU와 관련 장비를 확보해 미국 내 지상 데이터센터를 구축하는 데 사용될 예정이다.

articles.title: Satya Nadella says AI-found bugs will make outages more likely

facts.text: Satya Nadella expects more outages like the one that took down Outlook last week, because AI now finds software flaws faster than companies can safely fix them.
A fix for a critical bank system used to get a week of testing. Now attackers exploit flaws as soon as they surface, so fixes go straight into production.
Nadella also said the “floor of cyberattacks has fallen”.
He would ban models that reason in neuralese, an internal shorthand people cannot read.
Microsoft’s deal with OpenAI gives it royalty-free access to a frontier model until 2032, Nadella said.
“If you don’t accept the agent, somebody else will. If Amazon doesn’t, Shopify will,” Nadella said.
